aiUseDeclaration.statement: We used ChatGPT to help write some code.

applicabilityConditions.absenceDefinition: a species was treated as lacking a DFA if it had no DFA hit and also had more than 6,000 proteins in UniProt the criteria are liberal and likely produce false negatives, especially for species with far more than 6,000 proteins, so DFA prevalence across the fungal tree is probably underestimated
applicabilityConditions.note: conclusions are bounded by which traits had usable public data, not by which traits are biologically plausible
applicabilityConditions.phylogeny: TimeTree database web interface; the resulting tree represented 85 fungal orders
applicabilityConditions.proteinFamily: structurally divergent fungal actins, defined as ProteinCartography clusters LC04, LC11 and LC14
applicabilityConditions.statistics: model selection comparing a model in which DFA presence/absence and the trait share an evolutionary trajectory against a model in which they evolved independently, scored by Akaike information criterion where the lowest AIC wins phylogeny-corrected generalized linear mixed model (logistic regression) testing whether variation in the continuous trait accounts for variation in DFA status while controlling for shared evolutionary history; a slope significantly different from zero would indicate a correlation
applicabilityConditions.traitSource: Fun Fun: aggregates species-level ecological, cellular and biochemical trait information from multiple studies, including FUNGuild classifications of ecological function and trophic mode
applicabilityConditions.unitOfObservation: species, not independent observations; phylogenetic non-independence is modelled explicitly

confidence.basis: average cluster compactness 0.6 sits mid-range against 25 previous runs; cluster membership is the definition of the protein family rather than an independently validated boundary

cost.note: computational study; 853 species in the working set, 102 analysed; no monetary or compute cost is reported

entities.label: human cytoplasmic beta-actin (ACTB)
entities.role: seed protein for the original ProteinCartography run

entities.label: divergent fungal actin (DFA)
entities.note: A cluster of about 290 proteins, overwhelmingly fungal, annotated as Actin-2 or actin-like, structurally distinct from canonical cytoskeletal actin and found in species that also carry a canonical actin. ATP-binding residues are conserved; residues required for polymerization are not well conserved.
entities.role: the protein family whose function is in question

entities.label: MMseqs2
entities.role: sequence clustering of the original cluster

entities.label: FUNGuild
entities.role: ecological guild and trophic mode classification

entities.label: TimeTree
entities.role: fungal order phylogeny and divergence times

conditions.compactnessContext: 25 previous ProteinCartography runs gave cluster compactness scores of 0.35 to 0.86, so 0.6 is a reasonable score

positive.note: cluster compactness is used as a quality measure rather than a control

effect.metric: divergent actin proteins in the extended set
effect.note: the six input proteins fell into clusters LC04 and LC11, together 407 proteins, of which 144 were new; 436 divergent actins spanning 412 strains, after combining LC04 and LC11 with the original LC14

evidence.label: The results: ProteinCartography identifies clusters of divergent actins

findings.informativenessReason: rule applies to negative and inconclusive findings only
findings.question: How many structurally similar divergent actins exist beyond the original cluster, and in how many strains?

conditions.kingdomAssignment: NCBI Taxonomy, with manual curation to clade level where UniProt reports no kingdom

effect.comparedTo: Metazoa, the next most represented kingdom, at 2%
effect.metric: share of the extended set found in fungal species
effect.note: 406 DFA proteins in 385 unique strains after removing non-fungal kingdoms

evidence.label: The results: The extended set still contains mainly fungal proteins

findings.informativenessReason: rule applies to negative and inconclusive findings only
findings.question: Is the extended set of divergent actins still overwhelmingly fungal?

target.label: kingdom distribution of the divergent actin family

conditions.verification: tBLASTn against genomes for strains with multiple hits

effect.metric: share of divergent-actin-carrying species with exactly one copy
effect.note: 16 strains had two or more DFA hits; for half, a single sequence had been annotated by different groups; for the rest tBLASTn could not resolve discrete genomic locations, likely low coverage or assembly quality; at least 95% of DFA-carrying species appear to have exactly one DFA

evidence.label: The approach: Taxonomic analysis of the extended set

findings.informativenessReason: rule applies to negative and inconclusive findings only
findings.note: For half the multi-hit strains the duplicates were the same sequence annotated by different groups; for the rest tBLASTn could not resolve discrete loci, which the authors attribute to genome quality.
findings.question: Do fungal species that carry a divergent actin carry more than one?

target.label: divergent actin copy number per species

outcomeSummary: 436 divergent actins spanning 412 strains, after combining LC04 and LC11 with the original LC14 more than 93% of the extended set is fungal; the next most represented kingdom, Metazoa, is 2%
provenanceNotes: The protein family is defined operationally as membership of ProteinCartography clusters LC04, LC11 and LC14. There is no sequence-motif or experimental definition, so the family boundary is a clustering decision.
question: Which proteins are structurally similar to the six representative divergent fungal actins, and in which organisms do they occur?

sources.label: A structurally divergent actin conserved in fungi has no association with specific traits
Fungal Divergent Actin: Trait mapping and function hypothesis

data.label: Arcadia-Science/Fungal-Secondary-Actin-Pilot-v1.0.zip
data.role: analysis code, divergent actin lists, species and trait tables

stages.label: ProteinCartography structure search and clustering
stages.method: search mode with standard parameters; 3,000 Foldseek hits requested per input protein, 6,000 total proteins per input; Leiden clustering on the all-versus-all structural similarity matrix; similarity by TM-score from TM-align, where above 0.5 suggests structural similarity and below 0.17 indicates unrelated proteins

parameters.compactnessThreshold: clusters with compactness above 0.6 treated as well defined

successCriteria: A well-defined structural cluster containing the input proteins, large enough to support a species-level comparative analysis.
title: ProteinCartography expands the divergent fungal actin set to 436 proteins across 412 strains
